title: PS5 Players Start Permanent Blackout Protest, Threatening GTA6 Playtime
description: Irate PS5 players around the world have started a permanent blackout protest against Sony by unplugging their consoles. This could impact the upcoming release of GTA6 and Wolverine.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## The PS5 Permanent Blackout Protest Begins

An unusual form of consumer protest is currently sweeping the gaming community. According to reports from gaming media outlet Push Square, irate PlayStation 5 players around the world have begun unplugging their consoles in a coordinated protest against Sony.

The blackout initiative was technically scheduled to officially kick off at 7:00 PM local time, but many participants have already started observing it ahead of schedule. The primary design of this protest is to directly reduce active user metrics for the Japanese gaming giant. Active users serve as a key performance indicator for the company's ecosystem, and the participating players aim to hit Sony where it hurts by cutting off this vital data point.

## Potential Impact on GTA6 and Wolverine

As the blackout gains traction, questions naturally arise regarding how long players can or will maintain the shutdown, especially with massive titles on the horizon. For months, the gaming community has been eagerly looking forward to blockbusters like Rockstar Games' *GTA6* and Sony's own *Marvel's Wolverine*. If this permanent blackout continues indefinitely, participating PS5 players may find themselves unable to experience these highly anticipated titles when they eventually launch.

At this stage, the overall long-term impact of the protest remains to be seen, as Sony has yet to issue an official statement addressing the drop in active user metrics. Whether hardcore fans will maintain their offline stance when the next generation of mega-hits finally arrives is a major question for the gaming industry.

## Editor's Take

Using active user metrics as a battleground is a clever strategy for protesting gamers. However, with monumental releases like *GTA6* on the horizon, it remains highly questionable whether players will truly stick to their unplugged consoles for the long haul. Time will tell if this digital blackout has staying power.
